prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” agent for every seller — the right agent depends on your property, goals (top price vs fast sale), timeline, and personal fit. I can help you find the best agent for you. To get started, tell me a few details, or follow the steps below.

Quick questions so I can make a tailored recommendation:
- What’s the address or neighborhood and type of property (single-family, condo, lot)?
- What’s your estimated price range or recent mortgage/assessor value?
- What’s your timeline to sell (ASAP, within 1–3 months, flexible)?
- Any preferences: top dollar, quick sale, low commission, local vs big-brand brokerage?

If you want to do it yourself now, here’s a practical plan and how to choose the best agent:

1) How to identify strong Pleasanton agents
- Look for agents who have recent, multiple sales in your neighborhood (not just citywide numbers).
- Check list-price vs sale-price ratio and average days-on-market for their listings.
- Read recent client reviews on Zillow/Redfin/Google and look for patterns (communication, negotiation, marketing).
- Prefer agents who can show a written marketing plan and comparable-market analyses (CMAs).

2) Interview questions to ask any candidate
- How many Pleasanton homes did you sell in the last 12 months? Can you share comparable recent sales?
- What’s your recommended list price and pricing strategy for my home?
- What marketing will you do (photography, video/3D tour, MLS syndication, targeted social ads, broker network)?
- How do you handle showings and open houses?
- What commission do you charge and are there any other fees?
- How often will you communicate and how (phone/text/email)?
- Can you provide references from recent local sellers?

3) Things a top agent should provide in writing
- CMA and pricing rationale
- Marketing plan and timeline
- Net proceeds estimate (after fees/closing costs)
- Contract length and cancellation terms

4) Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific sale price or timeline
- No recent sales in your neighborhood
- Poor or no online marketing (no professional photos, no virtual tour)
- Vague answers about negotiation strategy or references

5) Practical next steps
- Interview at least 2–3 agents and compare written plans.
- Ask each agent to provide 3 local seller references and at least 3 recent comparable sales.
- Get a signed agreement only after you’re comfortable with the plan and communication style.

If you want, I can:
- Research and give a short list of top agents/teams in Pleasanton based on recent sales and reviews (I’ll need the address or price range).
- Draft an email or phone script you can use when contacting agents.
Tell me which you’d like to do and share the property details if you want a tailored shortlist.
